ground_truth.location: Table 1, Panel A (RD Estimates), RD in PM₁₀ (Daily), column (1)
ground_truth.context: Table 1 ("Automating Air Quality Monitoring System and PM₁₀ Concentrations"), Panel A, column (1).  Non-parametric local linear regression discontinuity estimate of the jump in reported daily PM₁₀ concentrations at the date a city's air quality monitoring was automated; the running variable is days from the automation date, with separate slopes before and after.  Triangle kernel, bandwidth chosen by the Calonico, Cattaneo and Titiunik (2014) optimal bandwidth method.  No fixed effects or covariates.  Sample: all monitoring stations in the Wave 1 and Wave 2 cities with pollution data before and after automation, station-day observations 2011-2016.  Standard errors clustered at the city level.

cell.label: claude-code
deviations_manifest: rdrobust: R package rdrobust 4.1.1 with vce='cr1' + cluster=code_city as the equivalent of Stata rdrobust vce(cluster code_city); p=1, q=2, triangular kernel, masspoints='off', default mserd bandwidth.

geonear (ellipsoid) nearest-neighbour matching reimplemented with a WGS84 Vincenty inverse distance; nearest Wave-2 deadline station per Wave-1 deadline station, kept if <= 400 km, controls replicated per match (joinby).
City-day aggregation for the search data takes auto_date/phase from the station with the latest auto_date (gsort -auto_date); ties broken by station id.
cell.notes: Translated Prepare_Data.do (station_day, station_month, did_ddl_match, search_city_month) and Tables.do (Table 1 Panels A/B, Table 2 Panel A col 2) to R with data.table/fixest/rdrobust. attempt-1 was exploratory (column orders, timing; no RESULT lines). The single scored run (final) reproduced all 13 claims to the reported precision (e.g. 34.7, 34.9, 27.5, 64.7, 57.1, -0.005, 60.3, 31.4, 66.5, 0.24, N=176426, 11.03, 8.73); effective Ns and bandwidths also match the paper (e.g. 232,326 obs, h=263). No claim-comparison refinement was made.
